A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 4DPC2hat research, with matching authors, architecture, dataset, and original experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning and question-answering experiments, temporal-modeling and bootstrapping ablations, and qualitative examples in the main text and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds 4DPC2hat results on 4D-Bench in Tables 4–5. Those results are distinct from the video-model scores attributed to the benchmark.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains Point-BERT local/global tokens, bidirectional Mamba, language projection, and the same three-stage training and failure-aware refinement procedure. The newly documented annotation verification does not establish an algorithmic or architectural revision.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 adds evaluation on 4D-Bench objects, comparing their point-cloud sequences with multi-view video representations. Coverage remains dynamic-object captioning and the same five QA categories; no real-world or LiDAR evaluation is added.

E2.justification: New Tables 4–5 substantially broaden comparisons to video MLLMs: MiniGPT4-Video, VideoChat2, InternVL2, LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-Video, Qwen2-VL, Gemini 1.5, and GPT-4o variants. Their video scores are explicitly imported from 4D-Bench. The original PointLLM, ShapeLLM, and MiniGPT-3D comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added 4D-Bench evaluation introduces a separate protocol comparing point-cloud inputs with published multi-view-video results, reporting QA accuracy and additional captioning measures including BERT and separate GPT appearance/action scores. GPT-action uses a five-point scale. The original Objaverse evaluation, including 4,000 test objects and the 200-object GPT subset, remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds an annotation-quality analysis identifying counting-under-occlusion and fine-grained-action errors, and reports no systematic issues in a manually checked 10% QA sample. Existing temporal-modeling, bootstrapping, augmentation, and data-scale ablations, plus appendix qualitative cases, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new annotation audit supplies reviewer and sample counts but no uncertainty estimates or agreement statistics.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 add substantial benchmark results, including 4DPC2hat's GPT-action score of 3.662/5, action accuracy of 74.30%, and counting accuracy of 66.14%. These are additional results under the new protocol, not same-setting improvements over v1. Table 2 also changes ShapeLLM-13B's GPT-4 score from 53.43 to 53.34; the proposed model's original scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), token definitions, and the cosine-similarity failure-selection expression are unchanged. Neither the main text nor appendices introduce new proofs, theoretical assumptions, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a dynamic-point-cloud MLLM, the 4DPC2hat-200K dataset, Mamba temporal modeling, and failure-aware bootstrapping. The additional video-model comparisons do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds geometric ambiguity, occlusion, and cross-view inconsistency as explanations for video-model weaknesses and advantages of explicit 4D geometry. The conclusion newly identifies adaptation to real-world dynamic scenes and LiDAR data as future work, clarifying an applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix B newly document manual caption correction, at least three annotators per sample, and verification of a random 10% of QA pairs. This is additional disclosure, without establishing that the dataset was rebuilt. Training hardware and hyperparameters remain unchanged. The promised future dataset release is removed without replacement access instructions.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a substantial Video Large Language Models discussion covering video architectures, MVBench, and 4D-Bench, positioning native 4D understanding against multi-view 2D projections. Numerous additional citations broaden the literature coverage beyond the retained static-3D and point-sequence discussions.

P1.justification: Section 4 groups the original captioning and QA experiments under static-3D comparisons and introduces a separate video-model comparison section. Other edits include annotation-verification prose, acknowledgements, publication/contact information, and localized wording changes; most existing narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two compact benchmark tables and revises Figure 2 to depict human verification. Original ablation Tables 4–5 become Tables 6–7, and several plots and appendix figures move. The appendix figure contents and other existing visualizations are retained, with limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: The 4D-Bench comparisons broaden evidence beyond v1's adapted static-3D baselines, while Appendix B makes annotation quality control more assessable. These benefits are limited by sparse documentation of the added benchmark's sampling and scoring procedures. Removal of the dataset-release promise without access information is a small drawback, but the added empirical evidence and transparency support a positive net improvement.
